newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian unions want talks on Renault plant deal.
newsitem.headline: Belgian unions want talks on Renault plant deal.

text.p: Unions at the assembly plant near Brussels which French carmaker Renault wants to close said on Friday they wanted to re-negotiate a management proposal of new jobs and financial compensation for the plant's 2,900 staff.
"The social plan which is on the table is not worthy of its name," Raymond Smeulders of the CMB union told an assembly of workers.
"No sum will be large enough to compensate you for the loss of a good job," Georges Jacquemijn of the ACV union said.
Unions said the number and the quality of new jobs Renault had pledged to create as compensation for the closure of the plant in Vilvoorde were insufficient.
"Four hundred is far too few. We want a real industrial activity with a future, not a haphazard collection of little businesses," Karel Gacoms of the socialist union said.
Union leaders described such jobs as fitting tyres on wheels, maintaining containers and managing stocks of spares stocks, or the creation of a pool of mechanics as "phoney employment".
They demanded new negotiations with management on Monday.

Gacoms said the unions still had a strong trump card in the shape of 3.5 billion francs ($97 million) of finished cars they have been holding hostage in the Renault Vilvoorde car park since February 28 when the closure was announced.
"As long as there is not a decent deal, we are not letting go of those," he said.
Renault's proposal gives workers up to two years to find a job while remaining in "technical unemployment" on compensation of 43,000 francs a month.
A special unit would be set up to help them find work.
The deal also calls for early retirement for 522 people between the ages of 48 and 50, the spokeswoman said.
Workers taking redundancy would be offered cash bonuses averaging 900,000 francs and going as high as two million francs, depending on length of service.
Renault plans to set up a new industrial activity at Vilvoorde that would keep on 400 staff.
It did not give an estimate for the total cost of the deal.

The carmaker has set aside 2.8 billion French francs ($475 million) to pay for closing Vilvoorde, including the cost of a jobs package, reconstruction of the site and capital losses on investments. ($ = 36.12 Belgian Francs) ($ = 5.9 French Francs)
